about: Global Fashion Group is an e-commerce group running online fashion and lifestyle platforms in emerging markets, including Dafiti (Latin America), ZALORA (Southeast Asia and Hong Kong), THE ICONIC (Australia and New Zealand) and Lamoda (Russia, divested). Founded in 2011 by Rocket Internet and partners, it is headquartered in Luxembourg with operations in London. It listed on the Frankfurt exchange in 2019 (GFG). The stated London location matches its operating office. Consumer brands with solid regional awareness.

Baibu (Baibu, 百布) is a Chinese B2B online trading platform for textiles and fabrics, connecting garment makers with fabric mills and suppliers, with services such as sourcing, logistics and payment. It is based in Guangzhou, Guangdong, close to the apparel manufacturing base, and has raised funding of around 570 million dollars. Further data about scale or ownership is not available from the input. B2B marketplace with no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Baibu is a B2B textile trading e- commerce platform.

about: Carter's is an American apparel company specialising in baby, toddler and children's clothing, sold under Carter's, OshKosh B'gosh, Skip Hop and Child of Mine (Walmart) brands. It sells through its own stores, wholesale partners such as Target and Walmart, and online, with revenue near 2.9 billion dollars. Founded in 1865 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. Listed on the NYSE (CRI). Highly visible family consumer brand in North America, particularly among parents of infants.

GOAT Group is a Los Angeles-based online marketplace for sneakers, apparel and accessories, which sells new and pre-owned items from authenticated sellers, and owns Flight Club retail stores. Founded in 2015, it serves tens of millions of members worldwide, with offices in Los Angeles and a large operation in China, and is backed by Matrix Partners, Accel, and Alibaba affiliate-linked investors. It was valued at around 3.7 billion dollars in 2021. Strong brand among sneakerhead consumers.

MUSINSA is a South Korean online fashion platform, started in 2001 as a sneakers community and now Korea's leading fashion e-commerce site, selling domestic and international brands, with its own private label (Musinsa Standard), offline stores and a payment service. Headquartered in Seoul, it was valued at around 2.5 trillion Korean won and pursued an IPO. Backed by Sequoia Capital China, Sequoia-led and Kakao-linked investors. Very strong brand with young Korean shoppers.

KREAM is a South Korean resale platform for sneakers, streetwear and luxury fashion, run by Naver's Snow Corporation spin-off (Kream Corp.), allowing users to buy and sell limited drops with authentication. Launched in 2020, it is among Korea's leading resale marketplaces, with millions of users and heavy youth appeal. The input places it in Gyeongju, which probably reflects a registered address rather than the main office in Seoul. Strong brand with younger Korean consumers.
cb_desc: Kream is a sneaker and fashion resale marketplace platform...

about: ABLY is a South Korean fashion shopping app and platform, based in Seoul, that works as an open marketplace aggregating thousands of small online fashion stores, mainly for young women, alongside its own services and delivery. Founded in 2015, it has millions of users and has been backed by investors including SoftBank Ventures Asia. Funding of about 259 million dollars is shown. Strong brand among younger Korean female shoppers.
cb_desc: ABLY is a fashion platform designed to act as an open...

about: Nike is the world's largest sportswear company, designing and selling footwear, apparel, equipment and accessories under Nike, Jordan and Converse, through retail stores, wholesale partners and digital channels. Founded in 1964 (as Blue Ribbon Sports) and headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon, it has revenue of about 46 billion dollars and around 78,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (NKE). One of the most recognisable consumer brands globally, with large athlete endorsements and sponsorship deals in football, athletics, basketball and more.

Rocky Brands is an Ohio-based footwear and apparel company, headquartered in Nelsonville, with brands including Rocky, Georgia Boot, Durango, XTRATUF, Muck Boot and Lehigh safety shoes, selling work, outdoor and western boots through retailers and online. It was founded in 1932 and is listed on Nasdaq (RCKY), with revenue of about 450 million dollars. Recognised among workers and outdoor enthusiasts in the US, with modest national fame.

K-Way is an Italian outerwear brand famous for its packable, waterproof jackets, originally created in Turin in 1965. It sells through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale across Europe, Asia and the US, aimed at casual and urban consumers, and has been part of the Italian group BasicNet (which also owns Kappa and Superga) since 2004. Crunchbase lists a London address and funding of about $202 million. Strong consumer brand awareness in Italy and Europe.
cb_desc: K-Way Inc. designs waterproof, weather-resistant clothing an...

about: Neiman Marcus Group is the US luxury department store operator, running Neiman Marcus, Bergdorf Goodman and Last Call stores and online, selling designer apparel, accessories, beauty and home goods to affluent shoppers. Founded in 1907 in Dallas, it has around 36 full-line stores and a big e-commerce business, and was acquired by Saks Global (the combination of Hudson's Bay's Saks with Neiman Marcus) in 2024. Previously owned by Ares and CPPIB after a 2013 buyout. Strong luxury consumer brand awareness in the US.

Revolution Race is a Swedish performance outdoor and cycling apparel brand from Borås, known for multi-functional garments, mainly for mountain biking, trail running and skiing, sold direct-to-consumer online in Europe and elsewhere, with a stylish technical design. Funding is shown as around 1.8 billion Swedish kronor. Founded in 2011, it is an e-commerce focused brand with a loyal following among outdoor sports enthusiasts and some visibility in sports communities.
cb_desc: Revolution Race is known for Multi-functional garments..

about: Gabe's is a US off-price retailer, also known as Gabriel Brothers, from Morgantown, West Virginia, selling brand-name fashion, shoes, home goods and accessories at discount prices through well over 100 stores across the eastern and southern United States. A family-run company founded in 1961, it has raised about $175 million, per Crunchbase. Consumer value-retail brand with regional awareness in Appalachia and the Southeast.
cb_desc: Gabe's allows people to shop the styles and brands they lov...

about: Digital Brands Group is an Austin, Texas fashion company that owns direct-to-consumer apparel brands including Bailey 44, DSTLD, Harper & Jones and Stateside, selling online and through wholesale and a few stores. Listed on Nasdaq under DBGI, it has built its portfolio through acquisitions, with revenue around $15 million and heavy losses. Customers are fashion consumers in the US. Small niche brands with limited awareness.

Torrid is a City of Industry, California retailer of plus-size women's clothing, lingerie and accessories, selling through about 650 stores in the US, Canada and Puerto Rico and online, in sizes 10 to 30. Founded in 2001 as a Hot Topic concept, it was spun off and listed on the NYSE as CURV in 2021. Revenue is around $1.1 billion. Strong consumer brand in the US plus-size fashion market.

Giglio Group is a Milan-based fashion and luxury e-commerce services company that runs online stores for brands, also offering logistics and a digital media platform, with some Nasdaq listing history under GIGL alongside its Italian listing. Customers are fashion brands and retail shoppers. Funding of about 24.5 million is shown. Small-scale B2B2C business with limited consumer brand awareness. Current status of the listing was not confirmed.

KITS Eyecare is a Vancouver-based online retailer of contact lenses, eyeglasses, sunglasses and eye care products in Canada, which started as a mail-order contact lens retailer. Listed on the TSX under KITS, it was a small consumer e-commerce company with funding of about $27 million. Customers are consumers buying eyewear online. Moderate consumer awareness in Canada. Further details of ownership and scale were not confirmed.

Mulberry is a British luxury fashion house, founded in 1971 in Somerset, famous for leather handbags such as the Bayswater and Alexa, plus accessories and clothing, made largely at its Somerset factories. It sells through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale. Listed on London AIM, its main shareholders have been Challice (the Christina Ong family) and Frasers Group. Strong luxury brand in the UK and Asia, with a premium customer base.

Bizongo is a Mumbai-based Indian B2B technology platform for packaging and raw materials procurement, connecting enterprises with suppliers and delivering custom packaging to customers such as FMCG, e-commerce and manufacturing firms. Founded in 2015, it has raised about $335 million, with investors including Accel, Sequoia and Tiger Global. Revenue is from product sales and platform fees. B2B with moderate recognition among Indian industry buyers and little consumer awareness.

Max (formerly Max Stock, Max Fashion Israel) is a Caesarea, Israel-based retail and credit business; the input suggests fashion, retail and textiles, with total funding of about 350 million. The name is ambiguous: it could refer to the Israeli credit-card company Max It Finance or the fashion retailer. Which entity this is cannot be confirmed from the input. It is listed according to the source search. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

JS Corp is a Seoul consumer goods and fashion company, apparently the Korean listed fashion-footwear and apparel group, with 40 billion won of funding shown. The input does not give product detail, so identity is unconfirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Melon Fashion Group is a Saint Petersburg fashion retailer and manufacturer, operating clothing brands such as Zarina, befree, Love Republic and Sela across hundreds of stores in Russia and neighbouring countries. It is a consumer fashion company aimed at young women. The input shows large funding in roubles. A well-known Russian retail brand, in a sanction-restricted sponsorship territory. The group has an extensive store network and strong online sales. Its brands are well known to young Russian consumers.

Modivo is a Polish online fashion and footwear retailer, based in Zielona Gora and listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange since 2021, formed from eobuwie.pl. It sells shoes, clothing and accessories from hundreds of thousands of products from a wide range of brands, plus its own labels, to consumers across Poland and more than 20 European markets, and operates showrooms. Revenue is several billion zloty. Well-known online shopping brand in Poland and Central Europe, with growing recognition elsewhere in Europe.

NOBULL is a Boston-based fitness footwear and apparel brand, founded in 2015, best known for training shoes such as the Trainer and Ripstop Runner, tennis shoes, apparel and accessories for CrossFit and gym athletes. It sells online, through its own stores and retailers, and has sponsored the CrossFit Games. It has raised about $150 million. Strong consumer brand in the fitness community, with athlete endorsements and a cult following, and it has expanded into performance running and lifestyle product.

Reju is a Paris-based textile-to-textile recycling business created by Technip Energies, which uses chemical recycling (Regenyx technology) to break down polyester waste, including worn clothing, back into raw material for new fibres. It aims to run large regional recycling hubs, starting in Frankfurt, and customers are fashion and sportswear brands that want recycled content. Funding of around 135 million euros is listed. B2B sustainability technology, no consumer brand, though it works with consumer fashion brands.
cb_desc: Reju works on solving the problem of polyester waste

about: Signa Retail was the retail arm of the Signa Group of Austrian investor Rene Benko, based in Vienna, which owned and invested in department stores and retail businesses such as Galeria Karstadt Kaufhof in Germany, KaDeWe Group, Selfridges and online sports retailers. The Signa empire collapsed in 2023, with Signa Holding and Signa Prime entering insolvency, so the Signa Retail business was restructured and its assets sold off. Defunct as a group, though its department store brands retain high consumer visibility in Germany.

Topshop and Topman are UK fashion retail brands formerly owned by Arcadia Group (Sir Philip Green), which collapsed into administration in 2020. Their brands and online business were bought by ASOS in 2021 for about 265 million pounds, with Nordstrom taking a minority stake, and are now sold via ASOS and partner retailers rather than the previous high street chain. Topshop was a household name for women's fashion in the UK, with a global following, and the brand has been relaunched online.

Farfetch China is the Chinese joint venture of luxury fashion marketplace Farfetch, with investment from Alibaba and Richemont, aimed at bringing global luxury brands to Chinese consumers through a Shanghai-based platform and Tmall Luxury Pavilion partnership. It raised about $500 million in a 2021 deal. Farfetch itself was acquired by Coupang in 2024 after financial trouble. Brand recognised among Chinese luxury shoppers, though the standalone business is less visible.

about: Rothy's is a San Francisco direct-to-consumer footwear and accessories brand, founded in 2012, known for washable shoes and bags knitted from recycled plastic bottles and marine plastic. It sells flats, sneakers, sandals and handbags online and through its own stores in the US and in international markets. It has raised about $519 million and became a fashion brand with a loyal following of women. Strong consumer brand in the US, with a sustainability image.

Lingerie, apparel and loungewear brand founded by singer and entrepreneur Rihanna in 2018, headquartered in El Segundo, California. Sells through its website, a VIP membership program, and retail stores, and is known for size-inclusive designs and its Savage X Fenty Show on Prime Video. Backed by TechStyle and other investors with a valuation above $1 billion in 2021. Strong consumer and celebrity brand.

London-based fashion footwear and accessories company with brands Kurt Geiger, Carvela, Miss KG and Kurt Geiger London. Founded by Kurt Geiger in 1963, it sells shoes and bags through its own stores, department store concessions such as Harrods and Selfridges, wholesale partners, and online. Privately owned. Selling in the UK, US and online. Strong consumer brand in the UK, known for its eagle-eye logo and bright designs.

It is based in Les Herbiers, Pays de la Loire, with funding of 140 million shown in unspecified currency. Industries include apparel, children and consumer goods. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: London-based fashion e-commerce brand selling affordable women's clothing to young shoppers in markets such as the UK, Europe and US. Funding shown is $150 million. Online fashion brand with moderate visibility among Gen Z.

about: Luxury fashion group based in Shanghai, listed on the NYSE (LANV) after a 2022 SPAC merger, owning Lanvin, Wolford, Sergio Rossi, St John Knits and Caruso. Lanvin, founded in 1889 by Jeanne Lanvin, is the oldest French couture house still operating. Majority-controlled by Fosun. Sells in global luxury markets through boutiques, department stores and e-commerce, with revenue of a few hundred million euros. Consumer luxury brand with global recognition.

Nordic online fashion and lifestyle retailer based in Malmo, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, selling clothing, shoes, beauty and home products from many brands online in Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland and Germany. Founded in 2007 by Hermann Haraldsson, it also runs Boozt Beauty and a large automated warehouse in Ljungby, and sells both its own and third-party brands. Revenue about SEK 11 billion. Consumer e-commerce brand with strong Nordic recognition.
Mumbai-based Indian fashion sourcing and manufacturing company (PDS Ltd), supplying apparel to global brands. Listed on NSE and BSE. B2B garment supplier.

RxSight is an Aliso Viejo, California medical device company listed on Nasdaq (RXST), maker of the Light Adjustable Lens, an intraocular lens for cataract patients that can be tuned after surgery with a light delivery device. Customers are ophthalmologists and surgery centres. Revenue is over $150 million and growing. B2B medical technology with limited consumer awareness.

Li-Ning is a Chinese sportswear company, founded in 1990 by Olympic gymnast Li Ning, and headquartered in Beijing. It designs and sells sports apparel, footwear and equipment under Li-Ning, with badminton, running, basketball and lifestyle lines including China Li-Ning fashion. Listed in Hong Kong (2331) with revenue of about 27 billion yuan and thousands of stores. A very high awareness brand in China, with global sports sponsorships.

Skechers U.S.A. designs, makes and sells footwear and apparel under the Skechers name, spanning lifestyle, performance, running, walking, work and kids ranges, plus Skechers Hands Free Slip-ins. Sales go to consumers through wholesale, about 5,000 owned stores and e-commerce in over 170 countries, with annual revenue near 9 billion dollars. Based in Manhattan Beach, California and founded in 1992, it was listed on the NYSE (SKX) until 3G Capital took it private in 2025. It is a global consumer brand and a known sports sponsor.

Supreme is a New York streetwear brand founded in 1994 by James Jebbia, known for skate-influenced apparel, accessories and limited weekly drops under its red box logo, with collaborations with Louis Vuitton, Nike and The North Face. It sells to consumers through its own stores in cities such as New York, Los Angeles, London, Tokyo and Paris, plus online. It was acquired by VF Corporation in 2020 for 2.1 billion dollars, then sold to EssilorLuxottica in 2024 for about 1.5 billion dollars. A high-awareness consumer brand.

Future Lifestyle Fashions is a Mumbai-based Indian fashion retailer, part of Kishore Biyani's Future Group, operating apparel brands and formats such as Lee Cooper, Indigo Nation, Scullers, Central and Brand Factory in India. It sold apparel and accessories to consumers via department stores and e-commerce. It raised about 390 million dollars, including investment from Warburg Pincus. It was listed on Indian exchanges (NSE, BSE) but entered insolvency proceedings after Future Group's collapse and the failed Reliance deal. Familiar Indian consumer brands.
cb_desc: Future Lifestyle Fashions is an integrated fashion company

about: ABOUT YOU is a Hamburg, Germany online fashion and lifestyle platform selling clothing, shoes and accessories from third-party brands and its own labels in about 25 European markets, plus a B2B commerce technology business called Nuvola. Founded in 2014 by the Otto family, it listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2021 and was acquired by Zalando in 2025 for roughly 1.1 billion euros. Revenue was around 2 billion euros. A well-known fashion shopping brand with a strong influencer approach.

about: FabFitFun is a Los Angeles-based lifestyle subscription company that delivers quarterly seasonal boxes of beauty, fashion, fitness, home and wellness products to members, and runs an online marketplace and membership program with content and events. Customers are mostly American women. Founded in 2010 by Michael and Katie Broukhim, it raised about 262 million dollars, valued near 1 billion dollars. Private. A recognized US consumer subscription brand with heavy influencer marketing.

Style3D is a Hangzhou, Zhejiang software and services ecosystem for the fashion industry, offering 3D garment design, digital sampling, virtual try-on and supply chain tools for apparel brands and factories. Customers are fashion brands, designers and manufacturers. Funding shown is about 177 million dollars. It is private. B2B, with a strong presence in China's apparel sector and little consumer awareness.

about: Everlane is a San Francisco direct-to-consumer fashion brand, founded in 2010, that sells basics such as tees, denim, knitwear and shoes with an emphasis on transparent pricing and ethical factories. It sells online and through a handful of stores in the US. It has raised about 176 million dollars. Ownership changes in recent years are not confirmed from the input. A recognized US consumer brand, popular with younger shoppers.

about: Express was a Columbus, Ohio specialty apparel and accessories retailer selling fashion for young professionals through mall and street stores and online in the US, plus brands such as Bonobos, which it later sold. Founded in 1980 as part of The Limited, it was listed on the NYSE (EXPR). It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2024 and its brand was acquired by WHP Global and Phoenix Retail. Well-known US mall fashion brand.

Spinnova is a Finnish materials technology company based in Jyvaskyla that makes SPINNOVA fibre, a wood-based textile fibre produced by a mechanical process without harmful chemicals and with low water use. It works with fashion and textile partners such as Marimekko, Bergans and Suzano, and runs a production plant in Finland plus a joint venture with Suzano in Brazil. Revenue is still small and mostly from pilot supply. It is listed on Nasdaq First North Finland (SPINN). Innovation brand, low consumer awareness.

Careismatic Brands is a Sherman Oaks, California medical apparel company, the owner of Cherokee, Infinity, HeartSoul, Dickies Medical, Scrubs & Beyond, and Med Couture brands sold to nurses and healthcare workers through e-commerce, uniform retailers and hospitals. It was formed in 2019 from the combination of Strategic Partners and Scrubs & Beyond, owned by Hidden Harbor, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023, ending up with lenders. Known to healthcare workers, with limited wider consumer awareness.

Suominen is a Finnish manufacturer of nonwoven materials based in Espoo. It produces wipes substrates and other nonwovens for baby wipes, household and personal care wipes and medical products, with plants in Finland, Italy, Brazil and the US and sales to major hygiene and consumer products brands worldwide. Revenue is around EUR 400 to 450 million. It is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki under SUY1V. Crunchbase shows about 28 million in funding, latest in June 2026. B2B supplier with little public brand recognition.

VANCL was a Chinese online apparel retailer, founded in 2007 by Chen Nian in Beijing, that sold basic shirts and clothing directly to consumers and grew quickly before facing inventory and competition problems. It was one of China's best-known direct-to-consumer fashion brands during its peak, with heavy advertising and backing from investors like IDG and Kleiner Perkins. Crunchbase shows about $522 million raised by 2014. Name recognition in China remains from peak years.

about: Desigual is a Barcelona fashion company, founded in 1984 by Thomas Meyer, known for colourful, patterned clothing, bags and accessories for women, men and children. It sells through owned stores, franchises, department stores and online in over 100 countries, with revenue of about EUR 900 million. It is privately held by Meyer, who remains the largest shareholder, with funding of EUR 285 million shown from 2014. Strong consumer brand recognition in Spain and southern Europe, and a past sports sponsor.

about: Aeropostale was a US mall-based teen apparel retailer, headquartered in New York, selling casual clothing under the Aeropostale and PS from Aeropostale brands. It had around 800 stores at its peak, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2016. Authentic Brands Group, with mall owners Simon Property and General Growth Properties, bought the brand, which was re-launched. Crunchbase shows $364 million in funding from 2016. Once a major teen brand in North America.

TechStyle Fashion Group is a US membership-based fashion e-commerce company, based in El Segundo, California, founded by Don Ressler and Adam Goldenberg. Its brands include Fabletics athleisure (co-founded with Kate Hudson), JustFab, ShoeDazzle, FabKids and previously Savage X Fenty with Rihanna, sold online and in retail stores, with revenue over $2 billion. Customers are mostly women who buy via VIP membership. Fabletics has strong consumer brand awareness in the US and Europe. Privately held.

ThredUp is a US online resale marketplace for secondhand clothing, shoes and accessories, based in Oakland, California, founded in 2009, where sellers send bags of clothing and buyers shop through a website and app, including resale-as-a-service for retailers such as Gap and Reformation. It listed on Nasdaq (TDUP) in 2021. Revenue is around $300 million. Customers are mainly women and families. Strong sustainable fashion brand in the US with large advertising.

Barstool Sports is a US digital media company built around sports, pop culture and comedy, founded in Boston in 2003 by Dave Portnoy. It runs podcasts (Pardon My Take, Spittin' Chiclets), social channels, live events and a merchandise and apparel line, earning from advertising, sponsorship and merch. Based in New York, with a very large young male following. Penn Entertainment bought it in stages from 2020 and sold it back to Portnoy in 2023; Penn's sportsbook later became ESPN Bet. Highly visible consumer media brand.

TCNS Clothing is an Indian women's fashion company behind brands such as W, Aurelia, Wishful, Elleven and Folklore, selling ethnic and western wear through exclusive brand outlets, large-format stores and online marketplaces across India. Based in New Delhi, it was listed on the NSE and BSE after a 2016 IPO. Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail agreed to acquire a controlling stake in 2023, completing in 2024. Strong consumer brands within India, with limited presence abroad.

Bombas is a US direct-to-consumer apparel brand, started in 2013 by David Heath and Randy Goldberg, best known for comfort-focused socks, and now also underwear, t-shirts, slippers and sweaters. For every item sold it donates one to homeless shelters and community organisations, with well over 100 million items given. It sells mainly online and through selected retailers. Based in New York, it has raised about $150 million and is privately held. Strong consumer awareness in the US, driven by heavy digital marketing.

Mister Spex is a Berlin-based online optician selling glasses, contact lenses and sunglasses from many brands as well as its own labels, supported by physical stores in Germany and other European countries and online eye tests. Customers are consumers across Europe, and revenue is from product sales. Founded in 2007, it listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (MRX) in 2021. Recognisable consumer brand in German-speaking markets and parts of Europe in the eyewear sector.

Otrium is an Amsterdam-based online fashion outlet marketplace that lets premium and designer brands sell excess stock directly to shoppers at discounted prices, with the brands controlling their own pricing and assortment. Consumers use the site and app across Europe, and Otrium earns a commission and fees. Founded in 2017, it has raised about 133 million, with a 2021 round. Privately held. Growing consumer awareness in the Netherlands, Germany, France and neighbouring markets through online marketing.

about: Poshmark is a social marketplace in which people buy and sell second-hand and new fashion, accessories and home items through an app and website, with the platform taking a commission on each sale and shipping labels provided. Based in Redwood City, California, it listed on Nasdaq (POSH) in January 2021 and was acquired by South Korea's Naver in a deal worth about $1.2 billion, completed in January 2023. It has millions of active users in the US, Canada, Australia and India. Well-known US consumer brand.

Kontoor Brands is a Greensboro, North Carolina apparel company spun off from VF Corporation in 2019, owning the Wrangler and Lee denim and lifestyle brands, sold through department stores, mass retailers, Western wear shops and its own channels in the US, Europe and Asia. Revenue is around US$2.6 billion. It is listed on the NYSE (KTB). Wrangler is a long-standing rodeo and country music partner. Strong consumer brands recognised globally, and an established sponsor, notably of Professional Bull Riders and events.

Acuity Eyecare is a Dallas-based company providing acquisition and operational support to eyecare practices, forming a group of optometry and ophthalmology clinics in the United States. It supplies management, purchasing and technology services to affiliated practices so they can focus on patient care. Funding of about $287M was recorded in 2022. Customers are patients of the local practices and the doctors who join the group. Private equity-style platform with low consumer brand awareness, since patients see the local practice name.

about: Neurolens is a Coppell, Texas eyewear technology company that designs prescription lenses with a contoured prism, aimed at relieving eye strain and headaches caused by eye misalignment, particularly from digital screen use. It sells through eye care professionals in the United States and some other countries, using a diagnostic device called the Neurolens Measurement Device. Funding of about $186M was recorded in 2023. Customers are optometrists and patients. Healthcare brand known mostly to eye doctors, with growing consumer marketing.

Sight Sciences is a Menlo Park, California medical device company that makes minimally invasive glaucoma surgery tools such as the OMNI surgical system, and TearCare for dry eye. It sells to ophthalmologists and eye clinics in the United States, with insurance coverage supporting use. It listed on Nasdaq in 2021 (SGHT). The funding total of about $144M is shown as of 2024. B2B healthcare brand known to eye surgeons, with no consumer visibility.

Photobox is a London-based online photo products company offering photo books, prints, cards, calendars and gifts in Europe, with brands that have included Photobox and Hofmann, and the group once owned Moonpig. Consumers upload photos online and order personalised products. Founded in 2000, it was backed by Electra Partners and Highland Capital and went through a restructuring in 2019-20. Crunchbase shows $305 million funding in 2014. A well-known consumer brand in the UK and Europe, with a gifting focus.

about: Privalia is a flash-sale online fashion retailer founded in Barcelona in 2006, offering discounted brand-name clothing, shoes and home goods to members in Spain, Italy, Mexico and Brazil. The input gives Sao Paulo in Brazil as its base. It raised about $295 million and was acquired by French group Vente-Privee (now Veepee) in 2016 for around EUR 500 million, so it operates as part of Veepee. Consumer brand with membership-based loyalty across southern Europe and Latin America.

about: Versace is an Italian luxury fashion house, based in Milan, founded by Gianni Versace in 1978, selling ready-to-wear, accessories, fragrances, eyewear, jewellery and home products through boutiques, department stores and online. Its Medusa logo is globally known. Customers are affluent consumers worldwide. Owned by Capri Holdings since 2018, when it was bought for $2.1 billion, it was in turn sold to Prada Group in a deal announced in April 2025 for about EUR 1.25 billion. Very well-known global luxury brand.

about: Dafiti is a Brazilian online fashion and lifestyle retailer, based in Sao Paulo, selling clothing, shoes, sports and beauty products, including its own and partner brands, across Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Colombia. Crunchbase shows about $250 million raised. Strong consumer e-commerce brand in Latin America.

about: Grupo Netshoes was a Brazilian online retailer of sporting goods, footwear and apparel, based in Sao Paulo, selling major sports brands and its own labels via its website and apps across Brazil, Argentina and Mexico. Customers were consumers buying sportswear online. Founded in 1999, it listed on the NYSE in 2017 and was acquired by Magazine Luiza in 2019. Crunchbase shows about $215 million of funding. Well-known Brazilian e-commerce brand that now operates as part of Magalu.

Xiu.com is a Shenzhen-based Chinese online fashion marketplace that sold domestic and imported apparel, shoes, accessories and luxury goods to consumers, with brands and merchants listing on the platform and paying commissions. Crunchbase shows about $150 million raised, the latest round in 2015, and it positioned itself as a leading global fashion platform. It was an early player in cross-border fashion e-commerce but was overshadowed by larger platforms such as Tmall and JD.com, and its current activity is unclear.

about: Ted Baker is a London fashion brand founded in 1988 in Glasgow by Ray Kelvin, known for tailored menswear, womenswear, accessories and fragrances with a quirky British style, sold through its own shops, department stores and online in dozens of countries. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange until Authentic Brands Group bought it in 2022 for about 211 million pounds, and the retail business then ran into financial trouble, closing stores in the UK and the US. Retail operations now sit with licensing partners. A well-known premium fashion name.

FIGS is a Santa Monica direct-to-consumer healthcare apparel brand, founded in 2013 by Heather Hasson and Trina Spear, selling medical scrubs, lab coats, underscrubs and everyday wear to nurses, doctors, dentists and vets, mainly online across the US and in other countries.
